about.title: Milpitas Car Accident Claims
about.longDescription: Milpitas sits where I-880, I-680 and Route 237 meet, and much of the city's driving happens on or near those three corridors. Public collision records for 2025 show 243 injury crashes here, 318 people hurt, and 4 lives lost. Reports cluster on Thursday evenings between 5 and 7 p.m., when commuters are heading home. If you were one of those people, the paperwork that follows can feel heavier than the crash itself. LawProactive is not a law firm. We are a free service that matches you with an independent personal injury attorney who handles car accident claims in Santa Clara County. That attorney works on contingency, so there is no fee unless your case produces a recovery. California gives you two years to file most claims, and only six months in some situations involving a public agency. Before you speak with the other driver's insurer, it helps to understand your options, hold onto your records, and let someone review the facts with you.

whyChoose.title: Why Milpitas Drivers Turn to LawProactive

items.title: Pure comparative fault works in your favor
items.desc: California lets you recover even if you share some blame; your compensation is simply reduced by your percentage of fault. An attorney can push back when an insurer tries to inflate your share.

items.title: Deadlines are shorter than most people expect
items.desc: You generally have two years to file, but a claim involving a city, county or state vehicle may need to be filed within six months. Getting connected early keeps those doors open.

items.title: No fee unless there is a recovery
items.desc: Every attorney in our network handles car accident cases on contingency, and our matching service costs nothing. You can also skip the other insurer's recorded statement until you've had a chance to talk it through.

items.question: The other driver's insurance adjuster keeps calling. Do I have to give a recorded statement?
items.answer: No. You are not required to give a recorded statement to another driver's insurer, and doing so early can lock you into details before you know the full extent of your injuries. It is reasonable to say you will get back to them after speaking with an attorney. Keep the adjuster's name and number and let your attorney handle the contact.

items.question: I was rear-ended on Route 237 near the I-880 interchange. What should I gather now?
items.answer: Save photos of the vehicles, the roadway and your injuries, and request the CHP or Milpitas Police report number if one was taken. Write down what you remember about the traffic, the time of day and any witnesses while it is fresh. Keep every medical bill and visit summary, along with proof of missed work. Those records become the foundation of a claim, and an attorney can help fill in what's missing.

items.question: Does California limit how much I can recover for pain and suffering after a car crash?
items.answer: For a standard car accident claim, California does not cap non-economic damages such as pain, suffering or loss of enjoyment of life. What you can actually recover depends on the evidence, the available insurance and how fault is divided. An attorney can explain what applies to your situation without making promises about a number.
